+def apply_merges(ids, merges):
+    """
+    Repeatedly merge the pair with the lowest merge index until none applies.
+    Same result as min() over get_stats(ids) keyed by merges.get(p, inf): the
+    rank list is in position order, so .index() finds the first-seen pair
+    among the minimal ones, and the minimal rank is the merged token itself.
+    """
+    merges_get = merges.get
+    inf = float("inf")

+        if idx == inf:
+            break # nothing else can be merged anymore
+        j = ranks.index(idx)
+        ids = merge(ids, (ids[j], ids[j+1]), idx)
+    return ids

actions.reason: Encoding loop (RegexTokenizer._encode_chunk and BasicTokenizer.encode) now uses a shared base.apply_merges: per step it builds the rank list with C-level map(merges.get, zip(ids, ids[1:]), repeat(inf)), takes min() and locates the first position via list.index, instead of building a get_stats dict and running min() with a Python lambda key. Equivalent: ranks are in position order so the first minimal position is the first-seen pair with the lowest rank (same tie-break as min over the insertion-ordered dict), and the minimal rank is exactly merges[pair]; inf means no merge applies. encode_ir ratio 0.753, equivalence identical, tests pass.
